subject: Snapshot transfer, proof-of-access & license scope for private deployment
messages:
From: Mike Carter <mike.carter@medsys.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: snapshot transfer & proof-of-access requirements

Rafael —

Thanks for taking this. We're getting the procurement and security teams lined up for a private deployment pilot at MedSys (single datacenter, in our AWS account). Before we commit to the Order Form we need clarity on the snapshot transfer and what you can provide for auditor-friendly proof-of-access. High level asks from our SOC2 lead:

- How do snapshots leave Redwood infrastructure (S3 presigned URL / encrypted transfer / direct VPN pull)?
- Can you provide chain-of-custody metadata (checksum, origin timestamp, operator identity) that we can hand to our auditor?
- Is there a mechanism to verify snapshots were taken from a specific model version and that the KV/prefix cache was excluded?
- If we require a time-limited license for the runtime only (no perpetual rights), what redlines should appear in the MSA Addendum?

We're also evaluating whether to ask for an escrow-like custody step (third-party holding snapshot until acceptance). Not ideal, but our compliance team will push for it unless you can provide equivalent controls.

Can you share a runbook or draft addendum we can review? Target timeline: aim to have procurement sign-off in 2-3 weeks if we can agree scope quickly.

Thanks —
Mike
Mike Carter
Director, IT Security
MedSys Health Solutions

Attachments: none
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Carter <mike.carter@medsys.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: snapshot transfer & proof-of-access requirements

Mike —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps below.

- Transport: we support presigned S3 uploads (mutual TLS optional), direct SFTP over customer-managed VPN, and a signed manifest with checksums. We generally avoid physical courier for security and latency.
- Chain-of-custody: we can emit an audit bundle that includes checksum (SHA256), origin host id, timestamp, model version hash, and the operator session id for the transfer. That bundle is packaged as a signed JSON and can be exported to your audit team.
- Snapshot contents: the standard snapshot excludes ephemeral KV caches by default; we can include custom artifacts on request (requires explicit scoping in the addendum).
- License scope: we can offer a time-limited runtime license for the on-prem deployment. Legal will propose language limiting deployment to the specified environment and prohibiting redistribution.

Attachments I'm sharing for review: snapshot-runbook-v1.pdf (transfer steps + verification checklist) and redwood-privdeploy-addendum-draft.docx (MSA Addendum skeleton). See links below; I'll also loop legal and solutions to finalize redlines.

Proposed next steps:
1) Lauren to propose minimal redlines needed for the MSA Addendum (legal items).
2) Camila to confirm transport of choice and network requirements.
3) Quick call with MedSys + Cyberscan (if you want a third-party witness) to walk the runbook and signoff checklist.

Can we pencil in Thurs 24 Jun 10:00 PT for a 30-min sync? If that doesn't work, send preferred times.

Best,
Rafael
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: snapshot-runbook-v1.pdf, redwood-privdeploy-addendum-draft.docx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private deployment: snapshot transfer & proof-of-access requirements

Mike / Rafael —

I reviewed Rafael's draft addendum. A few legal guardrails we should confirm up front so the commercial team can map redlines:

- License scope: confirm whether MedSys wants (a) runtime-only license limited to the named environment and timebox, or (b) operator/transfer rights that permit you to persist snapshots outside the named environment. Option (b) requires additional indemnities and audit windows.
- Audit & access: specify audit frequency and whether audits can be supported by us providing the audit bundle or require a live third-party access window to our control plane.
- Data handling: require that any snapshot that contains customer data be encrypted with customer-managed KMS and that Redwood deletes any intermediate copies within X days.
- Escrow/third-party custody: if MedSys insists, we need explicit liability allocation and acceptance criteria for the escrow recipient; we prefer to provide cryptographic proof of snapshot integrity instead of physical escrow.
- Operator access: define a maximum operator session window and require MFA + recorded session logs for any support sessions that touch the snapshot pipeline.

If you can confirm the answers on the license scope and whether you want a third-party custody option, we can produce a redline within 48 business hours.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Mike —

Quick technical note on transport and verification options (so procurement knows tradeoffs):

Options we support (ranked by security & audit friendliness):
1) Encrypted S3 transfer with pre-signed PUT + KMS envelope keys (recommended). We provide SHA256 checksum + signed manifest. Minimal network changes on your side.
2) rsync over customer-managed VPN with mutual TLS and our service account (good for high throughput; requires VPN peering).
3) Direct pull by your systems from our S3 (we generate time-limited credentials).

We can also spin up a one-time ephemeral transfer VM in your VPC that pulls the snapshot and immediately performs integrity verification with your auditor. That VM is ephemeral and access is auditable.

We attach a network topology diagram to show ports and egress rules (network-topology-diagram.png). A few practical constraints:
- Snapshot size will likely require multipart transfers for >100GB.
- If you want KV exclusions, we need the exact include/exclude list before snapshot creation; changing that midstream will require a re-snapshot.
- For KMS-integration, we support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via AWS KMS but will need a short key policy update to allow the transfer principle.

Mike / team —

Thanks for the input. Condensed next steps & timeline so procurement has a single artifact to act on:

1) MedSys confirms transport preference (we recommend encrypted S3 presigned PUT + BYOK). Reply with: S3 / VPN / Ephemeral-VM.
2) Legal scope: MedSys to confirm license preference: runtime-only limited to the named environment OR runtime + transfer rights. If you pick transfer rights, expect 2-3 additional commercial redlines (indemnity, retention limits, audit windows).
3) Redwood will produce a redline to the Addendum within 48 business hours after Lauren gets confirmation on #2.
4) Technical dry-run: schedule an Ephemeral-VM transfer test with Cyberscan as witness (optional) — target window week of Jul 12. Test will include: checksum verification, KMS encryption, tamper-proof manifest.
5) Final sign-off: target date Jul 23 for completed addendum + transfer runbook, assuming the above is accepted.

If you want Redwood to execute a third-party escrow holding flow instead of the manifest approach, we'll need: escrow recipient details, acceptance criteria, and a liability cap provision in the Addendum. We prefer cryptographic proof + audit bundle as it meets most SOC2 auditor expectations and avoids physical custody.

Please confirm preferences by end of week so we can lock the July timelines. I'll circulate a DocuSign link for the prepared Addendum draft once Lauren's redline is in.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
